parts.text:
6
A cyclist pedals along a raised horizontal track. At the end of the track, he travels horizontally into
the air and onto a track that is vertically 2.0 m lower.
v
higher horizontal track
2.0 m
lower horizontal track
6.0 m
The cyclist travels a horizontal distance of 6.0 m in the air. Air resistance is negligible.
What is the horizontal velocity v of the cyclist at the end of the higher track?
A
6.3 m s–1
B
9.4 m s–1
C
9.9 m s–1
D
15 m s–1

hints: Notice the cyclist leaves horizontally, so initial vertical velocity is zero while initial horizontal velocity is $v$, and the two motions share the same time of flight.
Use the vertical drop of $2.0\text{ m}$ with $s = \frac{1}{2}gt^2$ to find how long the cyclist is in the air.
Use the horizontal range of $6.0\text{ m}$ with constant horizontal velocity, $x = vt$, and your time from the vertical motion to find $v$.
walkthrough: Separate the motion: horizontally velocity stays at $v$ because air resistance is negligible, while vertically the cyclist starts from rest and accelerates at $g = 9.81\text{ m s}^{-2}$ through $2.0\text{ m}$.
Find the time of flight $t$ from vertical motion using $s = u_y t + \frac{1}{2}gt^2$ with $u_y = 0$ and $s = 2.0\text{ m}$.
Use horizontal motion at constant velocity: $x = vt$ with $x = 6.0\text{ m}$, so $v = x/t$.
Substitute: $v = 6.0 / 0.64 \approx 9.4\text{ m s}^{-1}$ with unit check $\text{m}/\text{s} = \text{m s}^{-1}$. This is option B.

A.explanation: At $6.3\text{ m s}^{-1}$ the cyclist would travel only about $4.0\text{ m}$ horizontally during the time needed to fall $2.0\text{ m}$, so cannot reach $6.0\text{ m}$.

B.explanation: The $0.64\text{ s}$ fall time for $2.0\text{ m}$ gives $v = 6.0/0.64 \approx 9.4\text{ m s}^{-1}$, which exactly covers the $6.0\text{ m}$ range.

C.explanation: At $9.9\text{ m s}^{-1}$ the cyclist would travel about $6.3\text{ m}$ in the $0.64\text{ s}$ fall time, overshooting the observed $6.0\text{ m}$ landing point.

D.explanation: At $15\text{ m s}^{-1}$ the $6.0\text{ m}$ flight takes only $0.40\text{ s}$, in which the vertical drop is only about $0.78\text{ m}$, not $2.0\text{ m}$.
